title: Unshakable Justice
subtitle: Facing the firing squad, you must hold onto your dignity, even as a traitor.

trails.title: Instructions in Advance
trails.description: A joyful goodbye letter, a solid paperweight.

content.text:
Greetings!

By the time you read this letter, I will already be on an auto island far out at sea. Oh! Please don't misunderstand, I adore your company, especially the hallway walking parties at 3 a.m. Though I do love all parties, walking parties are a particular treat, but unfortunately, The Lady's Code of Conduct dictate that I should be sound asleep by 9 p.m. What a pity.

Also, please tell Ms. Moissan not to worry! I'm not adventuring alone; miss Vertin is also going on a trip to the legendary El Dorado. The City of Gold! Magic, gold, and even bouncing coffee beans! I can't wait to talk to the locals about potential invigorating potion recipes!

Speaking of invigorating potions, now everyone can become a brewing master! All it takes is a cup of coffee, and before drinking, add three grams of gold, and voilà, you've got an invigorating potion! I've already prepared the ingredients—the gold is on the table! And thanks to the automatic coffee drip-beast in the lounge, we're saved from the hardest part—making coffee!

And do look forward to the special gifts I'll soon bring back!

Sincerely,

Sotheby

items.text: Tristes Tropiques
Unshakable Justice

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Cowards, mutineers, traitors!

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: You've made your choices; now you'll learn the consequences.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Zeno never forgives!

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Attention! Ready, aim—

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Fire!
Zeno Base

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: A shame you had to see all that.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Our Second Lieutenant Lopera is a crack shot. I trained her to be nothing less. Yet, no soldier of Zeno would take pride in an execution.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: The burden falls on me. This was my fault, my negligence.
The soldiers collapse, their limp bodies falling among the weeds.
Their blood stains the soil.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: She hunted down these traitors herself.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: M.E., check the bodies.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: The rest of you, form up!
The soldiers leave in formation amid the clearing smoke as the medics arrive to examine the deceased one by one.
Lopera hands the rifle to the attendant, removes her gloves, and turns to face Admiral Igor. He stands in the shaded colonnade, away from the blazing sun of São Paulo.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Orders completed, Admiral.
A rare smile flashes across the admiral's face.
He nods, a glimmer of approval for his adopted daughter in his eyes.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Well done, dismissed.
Lopera salutes before following the soldiers away from the execution grounds.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: There have been too many accidents—an unacceptable rate.
The admiral's face shows discomfort. The recent soldier desertions, like the leaked footage, have exposed the embarrassing state of the Zeno army.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What reason could you have to kill your own men?

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Not our men. Not any longer. They mutinied and killed their superior officer.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: So they got what they deserved, then.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Lieutenant Moldir is investigating still. We will find out who else was involved.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: The Apostles Brotherhood is back. We suspect they may have even infiltrated our base.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: We've also received intel indicating Manus Vindictae's presence in São Paulo.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Manus Vindictae?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm not entirely surprised. Intelligence suggests they are closely associated with the Apostles Brotherhood.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What I hadn't expected is that they would drop their "Order of Enlightenment" guise so soon.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But Arcana is dead.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: There is no room for doubt. No one, nothing, could survive a vacuum bomb.
It was the admiral's personal order to annihilate that once formidable woman. Destruction rained from the sky, and once the dust settled, it was clear that she had been utterly obliterated.
The sun glistens in the pooling blood of the executed traitors.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hm ...
Sweat gathers on her forehead.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: You will become used to the tropical sun in São Paulo.
The early summer heat here is overwhelming.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I've been through a lot worse.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Snowy mountains, deserts, and soaring eagles.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: I, too, find myself thinking back to those times.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: It should never have been a battleground.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Our business here is concluded. Timekeeper, Lieutenant Lilya, let us continue inside.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Do you really need me in there, Captain? Otherwise, I'd like to hang out here for a bit.
She gulps down some sweet liquor, but it provides little succor. It lacks the frosty flavor of the north.
This drink is lethargic, but it's all the base has to offer.
In São Paulo, soda is cheap, but rum is cheaper—and in near endless supply.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I'll check on Sotheby. See you both later, bye!

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Dismissed, soldier, but I caution you, much has been abandoned here. Remember our rules and keep to within the guarded areas.
Igor's Office
A simple office. Military papers litter the walls and shelves, and a phone sits on a side table. A few dice are scattered casually on the desk.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: There may be a person of interest to us nearby, a writer for the UTTU Magazine, said to be a blind woman named Urd. Her works seemed to be published after every era the "Storm" has affected.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: It could be this is only an alias, a pen name used by a new person each time, or—

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Or could she really have crossed the "Storm" eight times?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And, somehow, the "Storm" has never affected her?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Barbara provided us with some information.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: She said the latest piece was sent from a Veterans' Residence in São Paulo.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: I understand they have a doctor working there, a blind woman. If so, she would match our intelligence on this mysterious UTTU writer. You should seek her out.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: You are fortunate to have come now, Timekeeper. Carlos, the late commander here, was something of a pain to work with. An idiot. Maybe this is why his own men rose up and killed him.
He turns away.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: We've already dispensed with most of them.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Those men you just had executed?

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Yes. Lopera raided one of their locations. Manus Vindictae will not be so happy to hear that, I think.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: She was, I'm told, excessive in her work, a "loose cannon," but I am pleased with her results.
He seems to hold Lopera in high regard.
Cold, ruthless, decisive—qualities that don't quite match her sweet face and fiery orange hair.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Admiral, with you in charge here now, I thought I might ask a favor.
She needs to familiarize herself with the local area, transportation, and intelligence.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Things may become quite complicated during our visit to São Paulo. I wonder if I might request Zeno spare some manpower to assist us.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Our situation is more dire than expected. I will see what can be done, Timekeeper. But, no promises.
The seventeen towers and twenty-two courtyards of the base were once all fully patrolled, but now most of them are abandoned.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Lieutenant Moldir will provision you with everything you need.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: And Lopera, she knows São Paulo well. You may take her with you, as a guide.
The admiral has offered all the assistance he can spare. He sighs at the state of the base.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Now, Timekeeper, there is also something you might do for me.
He seems resigned. Zeno is just like this dilapidated base, a weakened shadow of its former self.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: As long as it's within my power, Admiral.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: I see that you have one of ours with you, Lieutenant Lilya—I ask that she serve us for the duration of your mission here. She is a fine instructor, and Zeno is in need of help training our latest recruits.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'll speak with her and see what she thinks.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Thank you.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: I should return to my work. Your comrades should be waiting for you in the meeting room with Lieutenant Moldir.
TO BE CONTINUED…
